audience.who: A developer or small-team operator who self-hosts apps and is often handling an incident alone
audience.job: Deploy an application with the right repository, branch and environment on the first attempt
audience.constraints: Keyboard use, slow connections, possible interruption mid-form

situation.where: At a desk or on call, usually in a dark room or a terminal-adjacent window
situation.initial_uncertainty: Unsure which settings are required and whether a deploy will touch production

intent.desired_feeling: In control and confident about what will run
intent.avoid_feeling: Rushed, or surprised by a deploy they did not intend

content.first_use: Show required fields first with plain labels and the target environment before the submit button
content.waiting: Say the deploy is queued, not finished, and show real status instead of an invented duration
content.failure_recovery: Keep entered values after a validation error and name the field and the fix
content.success: Show the deployment as started only after the server accepts it, with a link to its live status

visual.reason: Configuration and status matter more than imagery; faces or stock photos would add noise to an operational form

trust.claims: Never state a deploy succeeded until the backend reports a final state
trust.privacy: Do not echo secrets or environment values in messages or logs
trust.uncertainty: Keep a distinct queued/running state until a final result is known

audience.who: A developer or small-team operator who self-hosts apps and is often handling an incident alone
audience.job: Remove a deployment only when they truly mean to, knowing what is lost

situation.where: At a desk, often after a failed deploy and under time pressure
situation.initial_uncertainty: Unsure whether deletion is reversible and what data goes with it

intent.primary_action: Confirm or cancel deletion of one named deployment
intent.desired_feeling: Clear about the consequence and able to back out
intent.avoid_feeling: Tricked into a destructive click or blamed for a slip

content.first_use: Name the deployment and state exactly what is removed and whether it can be restored from the recycle bin
content.waiting: Disable repeat submission while the request is in flight and say it is working
content.failure_recovery: If deletion fails, say nothing was removed and offer retry or cancel
content.success: Confirm what was removed and where to restore it, only after the server confirms

visual.reason: A plain confirmation reads as honest and serious; decoration would distract from the consequence

trust.claims: Do not claim data is permanently gone if it is only in the recycle bin
trust.privacy: Show only the deployment name and essential counts
trust.uncertainty: Say deletion is unconfirmed until the server responds

audience.who: Any authorised user returning to the panel, possibly on a shared or unfamiliar machine
audience.job: Sign in quickly and recover access if a credential or second factor is lost
audience.constraints: Password managers, screen readers, shared devices

situation.initial_uncertainty: Unsure whether the account is locked or the credentials are wrong

intent.primary_action: Sign in, or reach a safe recovery path
intent.desired_feeling: Welcomed, secure and not locked out
intent.avoid_feeling: Accused of a mistake or left guessing why access failed

content.first_use: Show one clear form with labelled fields, a visible password reveal and a recovery link
content.waiting: Say the sign-in is being checked without inventing a duration
content.failure_recovery: Give a specific, non-leaking error and keep the username; link to reset and two-factor recovery
content.success: Move straight to the panel or the second-factor step

visual.reason: A sign-in form needs focus and speed; imagery adds nothing to the job

trust.claims: Never reveal whether an account exists
trust.privacy: Never expose which of username or password was wrong
trust.uncertainty: Treat lockout and rate-limit as explicit states with time guidance from the server

audience.who: A developer or small-team operator who self-hosts apps and is often handling an incident alone
audience.job: See at a glance what is healthy, what is failing and what needs action
audience.constraints: Many tabs, intermittent attention, colour-vision differences

situation.where: Glancing between a terminal and the browser during a release or incident
situation.initial_uncertainty: Unsure whether a quiet dashboard means healthy or stale data

intent.primary_action: Open the failing deployment or service
intent.desired_feeling: Oriented and trusting what the numbers say
intent.avoid_feeling: Misled by stale data or alarmed by decoration

content.first_use: Lead with current status and anything needing action, with text labels in addition to colour
content.waiting: Show loading and last-updated states rather than empty numbers
content.failure_recovery: If data cannot load, say so and what was last known, with a retry
content.success: Show real counts and timestamps from the backend

visual.reason: Operational data is the content; stock imagery or avatars would compete with status

trust.claims: Do not show healthy when the data is unknown
trust.privacy: Show only the signed-in user's own deployments and data
trust.uncertainty: Keep an explicit unknown/stale state distinct from healthy
